sentences.text: <u>Compound sentences</u>
Use a comma to separate two complete sentences that are joined with a coordinating conjunction, such as and, or, but, or so.

contents.text: We saw a flash of lightning, and seconds later we heard the rumble of thunder.

header.text: When a coordinating conjunction joins something else, such as noun, verb, or adverb phrases, do not use a comma. As a rule of thumb, use a comma only if there is both a subject and a verb following the coordinating conjunction.

sentences.text: <u>Complex sentences</u>

If a dependent clause is followed by a complete sentence, use a comma after the dependent clause. These dependent clauses usually start with a subordinating conjunction, such as after, although, as, because, before, if, since, unless, until, when, or while.
